reason: E2 directly supports the existence and thermal decomposition of a crystalline single-source precursor yielding single-phase HEA nanoparticles, but it does not explicitly confirm the mechanism of simultaneous liberation/reduction or directly compare outcomes with a physical mixture of salts. E3 describes sequential decomposition from mixed metal salts, which indirectly supports the contrast, but it concerns a different material system (CrMnFeCoNi) and does not address noble metals. E1 is about oxide nanoparticles and does not conflict with the hypothesis as claimed.
premises: A crystalline single-source precursor can integrate multiple noble metal complexes with atomic-level uniformity.
Thermal decomposition of such a precursor in a reductive gas flow can simultaneously liberate and reduce all metal species.
Simultaneous liberation and reduction prevents sequential nucleation and promotes single-phase alloy formation.
Physical mixtures of separate metal salts lead to sequential reduction and phase segregation.
The approach is effective at moderate temperatures (around 500°C) and yields homogeneous nanoparticles.
